subject: Finstar MSA: jurisdiction & interim relief — coordinate legal redlines
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena@finstar.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: legal@finstar.com, samir.patel@finstar.com
Date: 2028-06-21T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Finstar MSA redlines — governing law and injunctive relief

Karthik / Laura,

Thanks for the call earlier. Attached is our redline to the MSA (focused on Sections 16–18: governing law, forum selection, arbitration carveouts and injunctive relief). High-level positions from our side:

- We propose California law with Santa Clara County courts as the exclusive venue for litigation.
- We will accept arbitration for certain contract claims but reserve court access for equitable relief (injunctions) and emergency preservation of evidence.
- We ask for an explicit interim-relief carve: "nothing in this Agreement limits Finstar's right to seek provisional or injunctive relief in any competent court."

We redlined language to reflect those positions — see attachment "Finstar_MSA_redline_20280621.docx". Please confirm whether Redwood can accept a broad carve for injunctions and proposed venue. If Redwood prefers arbitration-first, can we get a narrow carve that only permits temporary injunctive relief (limited scope and short duration)?

Elena
General Counsel, Finstar Payments

Attachment: Finstar_MSA_redline_20280621.docx (Track changes)

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Finstar MSA redlines — governing law and injunctive relief

Elena — thanks for sending. Laura/Logan, looping you in for legal and commercial signal.

Quick internal notes:
- Redwood's baseline: arbitration for disputes (AAA) with governing law = California. We typically avoid exclusive-court venue language to preserve residential arbitration efficiency and reduce global litigation risk.
- We accept carve for "temporary injunctive relief to preserve rights or protect confidential information" but push to limit to narrowly tailored, emergency-only relief and require notice to Redwood and expedited briefing.
- Venue ask (Santa Clara exclusive) is a concern — we prefer a split approach: California law + non-exclusive venue (Santa Clara or federal Northern District) or arbitration only.

Laura — can you propose compromise language that: (1) confirms California law, (2) provides an emergency injunctive relief carve but limits remedy/time/scope, and (3) moves general claims to arbitration? Also note procurement will need to know if this impacts our SLAs or break-glass ops.

Thanks,
Karthik
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@finstar.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: logan_wright@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2028-06-22T08:27:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Finstar MSA redlines — governing law and injunctive relief

Elena / team — thanks, reviewed the redline and sketched compromise language (attached) that aims to split the differences while protecting Redwood's operational model. High-level proposal:

1) Governing law: California (substantive law) but venue language is non-exclusive; Finstar may bring emergency motions in a California court for provisional relief, provided Redwood can seek to transfer or compel arbitration on the merits within 14 days.

2) Interim relief carve: "Notwithstanding the agreement to arbitrate, either party may seek provisional equitable relief in any court of competent jurisdiction solely to preserve the status quo or prevent irreparable harm; such relief shall be narrowly tailored, limited to a duration of no more than 30 days unless extended by the court for good cause, and the requesting party shall meet an expedited notice and meet-and-confer requirement with Redwood counsel prior to filing where feasible."

3) Arbitration scope: All contract and statutory claims go to arbitration (AAA, commercial rules), except for the limited provisional relief set out above. Costs: Redwood proposes each side bear its own counsel costs for any emergency motion unless the court orders otherwise.

We flagged operational concerns for Procurement: if Finstar files a provisional relief motion, we want a commitment to engage Redwood's incident channel and give us 24-hours notice where practical so we can triage (avoid surprise break-glass escalations).

Attachment: Jurisdiction_Tradeoffs.pdf (short memo comparing Santa Clara vs. non-exclusive venue)

Please review and tell us where you cannot accept the 30-day limit or the notice mechanics. Happy to iterate.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Associate General Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Elena Ruiz <elena@finstar.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: samir.patel@finstar.com, legal@finstar.com
Date: 2028-06-23T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Finstar MSA redlines — governing law and injunctive relief

Laura / Karthik — appreciate the thoughtful compromise. Finstar's position: we can accept California law and a non-exclusive provisional relief carve, provided the carve explicitly preserves our right to seek relief in any U.S. court where Redwood has operations or assets. The 30-day limit is acceptable but we need an explicit extension mechanism if facts show ongoing harm.

Two quick asks before we exchange a near-final:
1) Add a one-line preservation-of-evidence sentence to the carve ("including preservation of log data and account snapshots").
2) Confirm an expedited meet-and-confer path: 48 hours notice and 24-hour emergency response window from Redwood's incident channel.

If you confirm those we can accept Laura's language and move to signature routing.

Elena
General Counsel, Finstar Payments
